title: Gaussian mean preservation
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\theta\in\mathbb R$. For $x\in\mathbb R^n$, define
\[
u_\theta(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y),
\]
where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure. Then
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_\theta(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)=\gamma_n(A).
\]
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. For measurable $A$ and every real $\theta$, $\int u_\theta\,d\gamma_n=\gamma_n(A)$.
